claims.text: Spin-polarized DFT with an advanced exchange-correlation treatment such as DFT+U can reliably capture ferromagnetic ground states.
Advanced exchange-correlation treatment properly accounts for the delicate balance of exchange interactions.
The proposed method stabilizes the ferromagnetic state relative to nonmagnetic and other magnetic configurations.
The target is a transition-metal or correlated-electron system initially represented by a nonmagnetic or paramagnetic calculation.
Spin-polarized DFT with DFT+U is proposed as an improvement over standard non-spin-polarized DFT.
The comparison is to be performed at 0 K with identical structural and numerical parameters.
The spin-polarization term and advanced exchange-correlation potential mediate stabilization of ferromagnetic ordering.
Explicit treatment of spin degrees of freedom resolves energy differences caused by exchange interactions.
Introducing an on-site Coulomb interaction through DFT+U, or using hybrid-functional corrections, better resolves exchange-driven energy differences.
Better resolution of exchange-driven energy differences favors formation of a ferromagnetic state.
The improved method will predict a finite magnetic moment.
The improved method will predict a lower total energy for the ferromagnetic configuration than for the nonmagnetic baseline.
Non-spin-polarized DFT yields no or incorrect magnetic ordering because it lacks spin polarization and has inadequate exchange-correlation treatment.
DFT+U may be inadequate for extremely strongly correlated systems or systems near magnetic phase boundaries.
Extremely strongly correlated systems or systems near magnetic phase boundaries may require further corrections such as DMFT.
The predicted energy lowering and magnetic moment depend on the system and on the selected DFT+U or related method parameters.
Failure to obtain both a lower ferromagnetic total energy and a nonzero magnetic moment relative to the non-spin-polarized calculation would falsify the hypothesis.
